extracted.intended_audience: UK government communicators (GCS members), Heads/Directors of Communication, SCS leaders, policy communications teams and arm’s-length body communicators
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and delivered commitments for implementing the Government Communication Service (GCS) Strategy 2022–2025 across UK government communications teams, covering collaboration, innovation, professional standards and people development.

rubrics_metrics.name: World‑leading digital capability
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategic vision to achieve world-leading digital capability across GCS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied expectation to modernise digital skills, embed digital design principles in operating models, and deliver accessible digital content at scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data‑driven decision making
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of systematic data, insight and research to inform campaign planning and evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes monthly/weekly research and insight reporting, standardised data collection across teams, and evaluation frameworks with stronger standards for digital content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhanced professional standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Raise the professional standards for government communications (e.g., MCOM 3.0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frameworks should provide clear 'must/should/could' guidance while allowing operational flexibility; aim for sector-leading, practical standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaboration: stronger cross‑government communications strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Create and maintain a stronger cross-government communications strategy to coordinate activity across departments and ALBs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect central strategy and campaigns function, shared planning, and multi-year planning where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaboration: new central GCS operating model
rubrics_metrics.description: Design a new central GCS operating model to improve strategic coordination and service delivery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model should focus on strategy & coordination, standards & capability, and expert/shared services (central team functions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaboration: build stronger networks and improve governance
rubrics_metrics.description: Strengthen networks and governance across GCS (boards, advisory panels, location/regional networks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: GCS Board, External Advisory Board, Heads/Directors engagement, regional networks to increase local connectivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaboration: improve crisis planning and response
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve crisis preparedness with standardised protocols, toolkits and playbooks for cross‑government incidents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect a crisis communications toolkit and playbook, tested via simulations; emphasises pre-approved messaging frameworks and escalation routes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve digital, data and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Strengthen digital, data and content capabilities within communications teams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes design principles for digital content teams, digital capability building, and evaluation standards for digital content (see S019, MCOM 3.0).

rubrics_metrics.name: Harness technology to improve impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt technology (including AI) to increase impact and productivity while preserving public trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adoption must follow ethical frameworks and policies; includes tools like GCS Assist and Innovation Lab experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drive efficiency throughout GCS
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliver efficiencies across the service through modernised processes and shared platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: digitise PASS, multi-year approvals, allocate testing budgets to unlock productivity savings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain public trust through propriety and ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: Hold the highest standards of propriety and ethics when adopting new approaches and technologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes refreshed propriety guidance, mandatory training, and the GCS Framework for Ethical Innovation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop people and raise professional standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Invest in learning and development and create coherent career pathways and accreditation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GCS Advance (Apprentice → Leader), accreditation models, enhanced induction and continuous learning culture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attract, recruit and retain talented communicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve recruitment and retention practices to maintain a skilled communications workforce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes location strategy to move roles outside London, outreach and people branding, and talent/succession planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build functional leaders
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop strong functional and senior leaders across government communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bi‑annual SCS leadership events, leadership objectives aligned to strategy delivery, and bespoke leadership development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a diverse and inclusive GCS
rubrics_metrics.description: Embed diversity and inclusion across GCS practice and career pathways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliver a D&I action plan and mentoring programmes (e.g., Connecting Diverse Voices). Monitor outcomes and access across geographies and demographics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create careers across the UK (location strategy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Increase roles and opportunities for communicators outside London to build local capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target for one‑third of GCS roles to be based outside London; measure ministerial department roles outside London and local network impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardised crisis communications protocols
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt standardised protocols and response frameworks that can be quickly activated across departments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Toolkits should enable real‑time updates, pre‑approved messaging and clear escalation routes; test via simulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi‑year campaign approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce multi‑year campaign approvals to enable better long‑term planning and resource allocation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use where campaign cycles benefit (e.g., teacher recruitment); monitor time savings and continued assurance of campaign value.

rubrics_metrics.name: PASS process RAG assurance model
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a RAG (Red/Amber/Green) classification within PASS to streamline assurance and reduce unnecessary reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Green = no second stage assurance; Amber = no additional ministerial review. Track percentage green/amber and hours saved, ensure 99% of campaign value remains under appropriate scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monthly (and evolving to weekly) research and insight reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Centralise and share research and insight reports across teams to reduce duplication and improve audience understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports should reach cross‑government teams, inform campaign planning, and evolve to more frequent reporting for mission‑based campaigns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test, learn, scale, ethically
rubrics_metrics.description: Approach innovation by testing, learning, and scaling successful approaches with clear ethical guardrails.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocate a specific testing budget, document learnings and scale responsibly under ethical frameworks (see GCS Framework for Ethical Innovation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocate up to 10% of campaign budgets for testing innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Reserve a proportion of campaign budgets for testing innovative approaches to improve impact and efficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: up to 10% allocation to test new tactics; monitored for return on investment and scaled where successful.

rubrics_metrics.name: GCS Framework for Ethical Innovation (ethical AI adoption)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt an explicit framework to guide ethical innovation and responsible AI adoption across communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framework should sit alongside a generative AI policy, support 'ethics by design', and be internationally recognised (OECD‑noted).

rubrics_metrics.name: GCS Assist: cross‑government AI assistant standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a centrally developed AI assistant (GCS Assist) with specialised prompts and governance to support communications tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect usage metrics, accessibility prompts (6 specialised prompts), average time savings (e.g., 2.8 hours/week), and governance under the ethical framework and generative AI policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility by default (Project Spark)
rubrics_metrics.description: Make accessibility the default starting point for digital communications rather than an afterthought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliver accessible resources, BSL solutions for GOV.UK, accessibility prompts in tools, and measure engagement and cultural change indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: MCOM 3.0 modern communications operating model
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt MCOM 3.0 standards to bring clarity, consistency and digital expertise into communications operating models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the 'must/should/could' taxonomy, embed design principles for digital teams, and monitor use and impact (page view metrics cited).

rubrics_metrics.name: Update GCS evaluation framework for digital content
rubrics_metrics.description: Strengthen standards for evaluating digital content within the GCS evaluation framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include consistent measurement, standardized data collection and reporting to give Ministers confidence in delivery and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: GCS Advance learning programme and accreditation
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliver a multi‑level learning programme (Apprentice, Practitioner, Expert, Leader) and explore accreditation and LMS implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure uptake, cohort fills, Net Promoter Score, and financial savings versus external training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory propriety and ethics training
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement annual mandatory propriety and ethics training across GCS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training must include how to raise concerns and guidance on ethical use of new technology; track completion rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional Assurance and Support Service (PASS) reform
rubrics_metrics.description: Reform, simplify and digitise PASS to streamline campaign assurance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Digital PASS should integrate the RAG system, reduce duplicative reviews and speed approvals while maintaining standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create central Strategy and Campaigns function
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a central function within GCS responsible for strategy and campaign coordination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Function expected to standardise processes, oversee multi-year approvals and central strategy delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardised approaches to monitoring and reporting on campaigns
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop systematic processes for monitoring and reporting with standardised data collection and consistent measurement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Processes should give Ministers confidence in delivery and impact; tie to evaluation framework and data strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve spending controls to improve campaign quality and join‑up
rubrics_metrics.description: Be more assertive in using spending controls to improve campaign quality and align activity across departments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raise the bar on spending decisions and coordinate funding to enable joined‑up campaigns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify campaign SRO remit and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Articulate the remit and responsibility of the campaign Senior Responsible Owner (SRO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define escalation, accountability and oversight expectations for cross‑department campaigns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual GCS data collection (FTE/role and location)
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect annual workforce data across GCS including FTE/role data and location.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use data to inform capability reviews, location strategy and workforce planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and refresh propriety guidance including raising concerns process
rubrics_metrics.description: Update propriety guidance to clarify how to raise concerns and include mandatory elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure guidance covers ethical use of new technology and is accompanied by training.

rubrics_metrics.name: New funding model for core and discretionary GCS activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce a funding model where core central activity is funded centrally, mandatory professional development via levy/FTE charge, and discretionary expert/shared services are charged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model should sustain core functions while providing transparent charging for services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish virtual GCS Innovation Lab
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a virtual Innovation Lab to coordinate testing and scaling of innovative communications approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lab to support Project Spark, Project Assist development and cross‑government experimentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish an Innovation Strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish a GCS Innovation Strategy to codify approach to technology, data and ethical adoption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strategy should align with 'Innovating with Impact' and include ethics and evaluation components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set best practice for GCS digital communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Define and publish best practice standards for digital communications across GCS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include design principles, accessibility requirements and digital content evaluation standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish a GCS Data Strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce a Data Strategy to underpin data‑driven decision making across the service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strategy to be coordinated with evaluation, standards and data collection activities (S011, S019).

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop new GCS and SCS induction approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Design and deliver updated induction approaches for GCS members and SCS leaders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include face‑to‑face induction events, orientation to tools (e.g., GCS Connect) and networking opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and consolidate core professional frameworks and guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Review and consolidate leadership, capability frameworks, Modern Comms Operating Model, competency framework and Functional standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for alignment across L&D expectations and clear career pathways.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop secondments action plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a plan to expand and systematise secondments across departments for capability building.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use secondments to spread expertise and provide development pathways (completion by stated target date).

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop model leadership objective for GCS leaders
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a model leadership objective aligned to delivering the strategy for use in performance year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objective to be used in appraisals to align leader activity to strategic outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliver bi‑annual SCS leadership events
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish recurring senior leadership events to focus on strategy delivery and cross‑government coordination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Events should focus on delivery, shared learning and reinforcing professional standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create and publish a GCS people brand and outreach programme
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a people brand and articulate the GCS people offer, including outreach and employer branding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use branding to aid recruitment, local engagement with universities and wider outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review talent programmes and develop succession planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess existing talent and diversity programmes and produce a refreshed talent and succession planning strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to strengthen pipelines, diversity outcomes and leadership succession.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliver the annual Government Communications Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce and deliver an annual Government Communications Plan aligned to the broader strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan should integrate cross‑government campaigns, evaluation, assurance and funding models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use data to target and support departments to drive efficiencies through functional standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage GCS data to support departments and ALBs to improve efficiency and capability via functional standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work with capability review frameworks and standards to target resource and training support.
